L00001: WikiTableQuestions Dataset
L00002: ==========================
L00003: Version 1.0.2 (October 4, 2016)
L00004: 
L00005: Introduction
L00006: ------------
L00007: 
L00008: The WikiTableQuestions dataset is for the task of question answering on
L00009: semi-structured HTML tables as presented in the paper:
L00010: 
L00011: > Panupong Pasupat, Percy Liang.  
L00012: >   [Compositional Semantic Parsing on Semi-Structured Tables](https://arxiv.org/abs/1508.00305)  
L00013: >   Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL), 2015.
L00014: 
L00015: More details about the project: <https://nlp.stanford.edu/software/sempre/wikitable/>
L00016: 
L00017: TSV Format
L00018: ----------
L00019: 
L00020: Many files in this dataset are stored as tab-separated values (TSV) with
L00021: the following special constructs:
L00022: 
L00023: - List items are separated by `|` (e.g., `when|was|taylor|swift|born|?`).
L00024: 
L00025: - The following characters are escaped:
L00026:   newline (=> `\n`), backslash (`\` => `\\`), and pipe (`|` => `\p`)
L00027:   Note that pipes become `\p` so that doing `x.split('|')` will work.
L00028: 
L00029: - Consecutive whitespaces (except newlines) are collapsed into a single space.
L00030: 
L00031: 
L00032: Questions and Answers
L00033: ---------------------
L00034: 
L00035: The `data/` directory contains the questions, answers, and the ID of the tables
L00036: that the questions are asking about.
L00037: 
L00038: Each portion of the dataset is stored as a TSV file where each line contains
L00039: one example.
L00040: 
L00041: **Field descriptions:**
L00042: - id:          unique ID of the example
L00043: - utterance:   the question in its original format
L00044: - context:     the table used to answer the question
L00045: - targetValue: the answer, possibly a `|`-separated list
L00046: 
L00047: **Dataset Splits:** We split 22033 examples into multiple sets:
L00048: 
L00049: - `training`:
L00050:   Training data (14152 examples)
L00051: 
L00052: - `pristine-unseen-tables`:
L00053:   Test data -- the tables are *not seen* in training data (4344 examples)
L00054: 
L00055: - `pristine-seen-tables`:
L00056:   Additional data where the tables are *seen* in training data. (3537 examples)
L00057:   (Initially intended to be used as development data, this portion of the
L00058:   dataset has not been used in any experiment in the paper.)
L00059: 
L00060: - `random-split-*`:
L00061:   For development, we split `training.tsv` into random 80-20 splits.
L00062:   Within each split, tables in the training data (`random-split-seed-*-train`)
L00063:   and the test data (`random-split-seed-*-test`) are disjoint.
L00064: 
L00065: - `training-before300`:
L00066:   The first 300 training examples.
L00067: 
L00068: - `annotated-all.examples`:
L00069:   The first 300 training examples annotated with gold logical forms.
L00070: 
L00071: For our ACL 2015 paper:
L00072: 
L00073: - In development set experiments:
L00074:   we trained on `random-split-seed-{1,2,3}-train`
L00075:   and tested on `random-split-seed-{1,2,3}-test`, respectively.
L00076: 
L00077: - In test set experiments:
L00078:   we trained on `training` and tested on `pristine-unseen-tables`.
L00079: 
L00080: **Supplementary Files:**
L00081: 
L00082: - `*.examples` files:
L00083:   The LispTree format of the dataset is used internally in our
L00084:   [SEMPRE](http://nlp.stanford.edu/software/sempre/) code base.
L00085:   The `*.examples` files contain the same information as the TSV files.
L00086: 
L00087: Tables
L00088: ------
L00089: 
L00090: The `csv/` directory contains the extracted tables, while the `page/` directory
L00091: contains the raw HTML data of the whole web page.
L00092: 
L00093: **Table Formats:**
L00094: 
L00095: - `csv/xxx-csv/yyy.csv`:
L00096:   Comma-separated table (The first row is treated as the column header)
L00097:   The escaped characters include:
L00098:   double quote (`"` => `\"`) and backslash (`\` => `\\`).
L00099:   Newlines are represented as quoted line breaks.
L00100: 
L00101: - `csv/xxx-csv/yyy.tsv`:
L00102:   Tab-separated table. The TSV escapes explained at the beginning are used.
L00103: 
L00104: - `csv/xxx-csv/yyy.table`:
L00105:   Human-readable column-aligned table. Some information was loss during
L00106:   data conversion, so this format should not be used as an input.
L00107: 
L00108: - `csv/xxx-csv/yyy.html`:
L00109:   Formatted HTML of just the table
L00110: 
L00111: - `page/xxx-page/yyy.html`:
L00112:   Raw HTML of the whole web page
L00113: 
L00114: - `page/xxx-page/yyy.json`:
L00115:   Metadata including the URL, the page title, and the index of the chosen table.
L00116:   (Only tables with the `wikitable` class are considered.)
L00117: 
L00118: The conversion from HTML to CSV and TSV was done using `table-to-tsv.py`.
L00119: Its dependency is in the `weblib/` directory.
L00120: 
L00121: CoreNLP Tagged Files
L00122: --------------------
L00123: Questions and tables are tagged using CoreNLP 3.5.2.
L00124: The annotation is not perfect (e.g., it cannot detect the date "13-12-1989"),
L00125: but it is usually good enough.
L00126: 
L00127: - `tagged/data/*.tagged`:
L00128:   Tagged questions. Each line contains one example.
L00129: 
L00130:   Field descriptions:
L00131:   - id:          unique ID of the example
L00132:   - utterance:   the question in its original format
L00133:   - context:     the table used to answer the question
L00134:   - targetValue: the answer, possibly a `|`-separated list
L00135:   - tokens:      the question, tokenized
L00136:   - lemmaTokens: the question, tokenized and lemmatized
L00137:   - posTags:     the part of speech tag of each token
L00138:   - nerTags:     the name entity tag of each token
L00139:   - nerValues:   if the NER tag is numerical or temporal, the value of that
L00140:      NER span will be listed here
L00141:   - targetCanon: canonical form of the answers where numbers and dates
L00142:      are converted into normalized values
L00143:   - targetCanonType: type of the canonical answers; possible values include
L00144:      "number", "date", "string", and "mixed"
L00145: 
L00146: - `tagged/xxx-tagged/yyy.tagged`:
L00147:   Tab-separated file containing the CoreNLP annotation of each table cell.
L00148:   Each line represents one table cell.
L00149: 
L00150:   Mandatory fields:
L00151:   - row:         row index (-1 is the header row)
L00152:   - col:         column index
L00153:   - id:          unique ID of the cell.
L00154:     - Each header cell gets a unique ID even when the contents are identical
L00155:     - Non-header cells get the same ID if they have exactly the same content
L00156:   - content:     the cell text (images and hidden spans are removed)
L00157:   - tokens:      the cell text, tokenized
L00158:   - lemmaTokens: the cell text, tokenized and lemmatized
L00159:   - posTags:     the part of speech tag of each token
L00160:   - nerTags:     the name entity tag of each token
L00161:   - nerValues:   if the NER tag is numerical or temporal, the value of that
L00162:      NER span will be listed here
L00163: 
L00164:   The following fields are optional:
L00165:   - number:      interpretation as a number (for multiple numbers, the first
L00166:      number is extracted)
L00167:   - date:        interpretation as a date
L00168:   - num2:        the second number in the cell (useful for scores like `1-2`)
L00169:   - list:        interpretation as a list of items
L00170: 
L00171:   Header cells do not have these optional fields.
L00172: 
L00173: Evaluator
L00174: ---------
L00175: 
L00176: `evaluator.py` is the official evaluator.
L00177: 
L00178: Usage:
L00179:     evaluator.py <tagged_dataset_path> <prediction_path>
L00180: 
L00181: - `tagged_dataset_path` should be a dataset .tagged file containing the
L00182:   relevant examples
L00183: 
L00184: - `prediction_path` should contain predictions from the model.
L00185:   Each line should contain
L00186:     ex_id <tab> item1 <tab> item2 <tab> ...
L00187:   If the model does not produce a prediction, just output `ex_id` without
L00188:   the items.
L00189: 
L00190: Note that the resulting scores will be different from what
L00191: [SEMPRE](https://github.com/percyliang/sempre/) produces as SEMPRE also
L00192: enforces the prediction to have the same type as the target value, while
L00193: the official evaluator is more lenient.
L00194: 
L00195: Version History
L00196: ---------------
L00197: 
L00198: 1.0 - Fixed various bugs in datasets
L00199:       (encoding issues, number normalization issues)
L00200: 
L00201: 0.5 - Added evaluator
L00202: 
L00203: 0.4 - Added annotated logical forms of the first 300 examples /
L00204:       Renamed CoreNLP tagged data as `tagged` to avoid confusion
L00205: 
L00206: 0.3 - Repaired table headers /
L00207:       Added raw HTML tables /
L00208:       Added CoreNLP tagged data
L00209: 
L00210: 0.2 - Initial release
L00211: 
L00212: For questions and comments, please contact Ice Pasupat <ppasupat@cs.stanford.edu>

L00001: #!/usr/bin/env python
L00002: # -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
L00003: u"""Official Evaluator for WikiTableQuestions Dataset
L00004: 
L00005: There are 3 value types
L00006: 1. String (unicode)
L00007: 2. Number (float)
L00008: 3. Date (a struct with 3 fields: year, month, and date)
L00009:    Some fields (but not all) can be left unspecified. However, if only the year
L00010:    is specified, the date is automatically converted into a number.
L00011: 
L00012: Target denotation = a set of items
L00013: - Each item T is a raw unicode string from Mechanical Turk
L00014: - If T can be converted to a number or date (via Stanford CoreNLP), the
L00015:     converted value (number T_N or date T_D) is precomputed
L00016: 
L00017: Predicted denotation = a set of items
L00018: - Each item P is a string, a number, or a date
L00019: - If P is read from a text file, assume the following
L00020:   - A string that can be converted into a number (float) is converted into a
L00021:     number
L00022:   - A string of the form "yyyy-mm-dd" is converted into a date. Unspecified
L00023:     fields can be marked as "xx". For example, "xx-01-02" represents the date
L00024:     January 2nd of an unknown year.
L00025:   - Otherwise, it is kept as a string
L00026: 
L00027: The predicted denotation is correct if
L00028: 1. The sizes of the target denotation and the predicted denotation are equal
L00029: 2. Each item in the target denotation matches an item in the predicted
L00030:     denotation
L00031: 
L00032: A target item T matches a predicted item P if one of the following is true:
L00033: 1. normalize(raw string of T) and normalize(string form of P) are identical.
L00034:    The normalize method performs the following normalizations on strings:
L00035:    - Remove diacritics (é → e)
L00036:    - Convert smart quotes (‘’´`“”) and dashes (‐‑‒–—−) into ASCII ones
L00037:    - Remove citations (trailing •♦†‡*#+ or [...])
L00038:    - Remove details in parenthesis (trailing (...))
L00039:    - Remove outermost quotation marks
L00040:    - Remove trailing period (.)
L00041:    - Convert to lowercase
L00042:    - Collapse multiple whitespaces and strip outermost whitespaces
L00043: 2. T can be interpreted as a number T_N, P is a number, and P = T_N
L00044: 3. T can be interpreted as a date T_D, P is a date, and P = T_D
L00045:    (exact match on all fields; e.g., xx-01-12 and 1990-01-12 do not match)
L00046: """
L00047: __version__ = '1.0.2'
L00048: 
L00049: import sys, os, re, argparse
L00050: import unicodedata
L00051: from codecs import open
L00052: from math import isnan, isinf
L00053: from abc import ABCMeta, abstractmethod
L00054: 
L00055: ################ String Normalization ################
L00056: 
L00057: def normalize(x):
L00058:     if not isinstance(x, unicode):
L00059:         x = x.decode('utf8', errors='ignore')
L00060:     # Remove diacritics
L00061:     x = ''.join(c for c in unicodedata.normalize('NFKD', x)
L00062:                 if unicodedata.category(c) != 'Mn')
L00063:     # Normalize quotes and dashes
L00064:     x = re.sub(ur"[‘’´`]", "'", x)
L00065:     x = re.sub(ur"[“”]", "\"", x)
L00066:     x = re.sub(ur"[‐‑‒–—−]", "-", x)
L00067:     while True:
L00068:         old_x = x
L00069:         # Remove citations
L00070:         x = re.sub(ur"((?<!^)\[[^\]]*\]|\[\d+\]|[•♦†‡*#+])*$", "", x.strip())
L00071:         # Remove details in parenthesis
L00072:         x = re.sub(ur"(?<!^)( \([^)]*\))*$", "", x.strip())
L00073:         # Remove outermost quotation mark
L00074:         x = re.sub(ur'^"([^"]*)"$', r'\1', x.strip())
L00075:         if x == old_x:
L00076:             break
L00077:     # Remove final '.'
L00078:     if x and x[-1] == '.':
L00079:         x = x[:-1]
L00080:     # Collapse whitespaces and convert to lower case
L00081:     x = re.sub(ur'\s+', ' ', x, flags=re.U).lower().strip()
L00082:     return x
L00083: 
L00084: 
L00085: ################ Value Types ################
L00086: 
L00087: class Value(object):
L00088:     __metaclass__ = ABCMeta
L00089: 
L00090:     # Should be populated with the normalized string
L00091:     _normalized = None
L00092: 
L00093:     @abstractmethod
L00094:     def match(self, other):
L00095:         """Return True if the value matches the other value.
L00096: 
L00097:         Args:
L00098:             other (Value)
L00099:         Returns:
L00100:             a boolean
L00101:         """
L00102:         pass
L00103: 
L00104:     @property
L00105:     def normalized(self):
L00106:         return self._normalized
L00107: 
L00108: 
L00109: class StringValue(Value):
L00110: 
L00111:     def __init__(self, content):
L00112:         assert isinstance(content, basestring)
L00113:         self._normalized = normalize(content)
L00114:         self._hash = hash(self._normalized)
L00115: 
L00116:     def __eq__(self, other):
L00117:         return isinstance(other, StringValue) and self.normalized == other.normalized
L00118: 
L00119:     def __hash__(self):
L00120:         return self._hash
L00121: 
L00122:     def __str__(self):
L00123:         return 'S' +  str([self.normalized])
L00124:     __repr__ = __str__
L00125: 
L00126:     def match(self, other):
L00127:         assert isinstance(other, Value)
L00128:         return self.normalized == other.normalized
L00129: 
L00130: 
L00131: class NumberValue(Value):
L00132: 
L00133:     def __init__(self, amount, original_string=None):
L00134:         assert isinstance(amount, (int, long, float))
L00135:         if abs(amount - round(amount)) < 1e-6:
L00136:             self._amount = int(amount)
L00137:         else:
L00138:             self._amount = float(amount)
L00139:         if not original_string:
L00140:             self._normalized = unicode(self._amount)
L00141:         else:
L00142:             self._normalized = normalize(original_string)
L00143:         self._hash = hash(self._amount)
L00144: 
L00145:     @property
L00146:     def amount(self):
L00147:         return self._amount
L00148: 
L00149:     def __eq__(self, other):
L00150:         return isinstance(other, NumberValue) and self.amount == other.amount
L00151: 
L00152:     def __hash__(self):
L00153:         return self._hash
L00154: 
L00155:     def __str__(self):
L00156:         return ('N(%f)' % self.amount) + str([self.normalized])
L00157:     __repr__ = __str__
L00158: 
L00159:     def match(self, other):
L00160:         assert isinstance(other, Value)
L00161:         if self.normalized == other.normalized:
L00162:             return True
L00163:         if isinstance(other, NumberValue):
L00164:             return abs(self.amount - other.amount) < 1e-6
L00165:         return False
L00166: 
L00167:     @staticmethod
L00168:     def parse(text):
L00169:         """Try to parse into a number.
L00170: 
L00171:         Return:
L00172:             the number (int or float) if successful; otherwise None.
L00173:         """
L00174:         try:
L00175:             return int(text)
L00176:         except:
L00177:             try:
L00178:                 amount = float(text)
L00179:                 assert not isnan(amount) and not isinf(amount)
L00180:                 return amount
L00181:             except:
L00182:                 return None
L00183: 
L00184: 
L00185: class DateValue(Value):
L00186: 
L00187:     def __init__(self, year, month, day, original_string=None):
L00188:         """Create a new DateValue. Placeholders are marked as -1."""
L00189:         assert isinstance(year, int)
L00190:         assert isinstance(month, int) and (month == -1 or 1 <= month <= 12)
L00191:         assert isinstance(day, int) and (day == -1 or 1 <= day <= 31)
L00192:         assert not (year == month == day == -1)
L00193:         self._year = year
L00194:         self._month = month
L00195:         self._day = day
L00196:         if not original_string:
L00197:             self._normalized = '{}-{}-{}'.format(
L00198:                 year if year != -1 else 'xx',
L00199:                 month if month != -1 else 'xx',
L00200:                 day if day != '-1' else 'xx')
L00201:         else:
L00202:             self._normalized = normalize(original_string)
L00203:         self._hash = hash((self._year, self._month, self._day))
L00204: 
L00205:     @property
L00206:     def ymd(self):
L00207:         return (self._year, self._month, self._day)
L00208: 
L00209:     def __eq__(self, other):
L00210:         return isinstance(other, DateValue) and self.ymd == other.ymd
L00211: 
L00212:     def __hash__(self):
L00213:         return self._hash
L00214: 
L00215:     def __str__(self):
L00216:         return (('D(%d,%d,%d)' % (self._year, self._month, self._day))
L00217:                 + str([self._normalized]))
L00218:     __repr__ = __str__
L00219: 
L00220:     def match(self, other):
L00221:         assert isinstance(other, Value)
L00222:         if self.normalized == other.normalized:
L00223:             return True
L00224:         if isinstance(other, DateValue):
L00225:             return self.ymd == other.ymd
L00226:         return False
L00227: 
L00228:     @staticmethod
L00229:     def parse(text):
L00230:         """Try to parse into a date.
L00231: 
L00232:         Return:
L00233:             tuple (year, month, date) if successful; otherwise None.
L00234:         """
L00235:         try:
L00236:             ymd = text.lower().split('-')
L00237:             assert len(ymd) == 3
L00238:             year = -1 if ymd[0] in ('xx', 'xxxx') else int(ymd[0])
L00239:             month = -1 if ymd[1] == 'xx' else int(ymd[1])
L00240:             day = -1 if ymd[2] == 'xx' else int(ymd[2])
L00241:             assert not (year == month == day == -1)
L00242:             assert month == -1 or 1 <= month <= 12
L00243:             assert day == -1 or 1 <= day <= 31
L00244:             return (year, month, day)
L00245:         except:
L00246:             return None
L00247: 
L00248: 
L00249: ################ Value Instantiation ################
L00250: 
L00251: def to_value(original_string, corenlp_value=None):
L00252:     """Convert the string to Value object.
L00253: 
L00254:     Args:
L00255:         original_string (basestring): Original string
L00256:         corenlp_value (basestring): Optional value returned from CoreNLP
L00257:     Returns:
L00258:         Value
L00259:     """
L00260:     if isinstance(original_string, Value):
L00261:         # Already a Value
L00262:         return original_string
L00263:     if not corenlp_value:
L00264:         corenlp_value = original_string
L00265:     # Number?
L00266:     amount = NumberValue.parse(corenlp_value)
L00267:     if amount is not None:
L00268:         return NumberValue(amount, original_string)
L00269:     # Date?
L00270:     ymd = DateValue.parse(corenlp_value)
L00271:     if ymd is not None:
L00272:         if ymd[1] == ymd[2] == -1:
L00273:             return NumberValue(ymd[0], original_string)
L00274:         else:
L00275:             return DateValue(ymd[0], ymd[1], ymd[2], original_string)
L00276:     # String.
L00277:     return StringValue(original_string)
L00278: 
L00279: def to_value_list(original_strings, corenlp_values=None):
L00280:     """Convert a list of strings to a list of Values
L00281: 
L00282:     Args:
L00283:         original_strings (list[basestring])
L00284:         corenlp_values (list[basestring or None])
L00285:     Returns:
L00286:         list[Value]
L00287:     """
L00288:     assert isinstance(original_strings, (list, tuple, set))
L00289:     if corenlp_values is not None:
L00290:         assert isinstance(corenlp_values, (list, tuple, set))
L00291:         assert len(original_strings) == len(corenlp_values)
L00292:         return list(set(to_value(x, y) for (x, y)
L00293:                 in zip(original_strings, corenlp_values)))
L00294:     else:
L00295:         return list(set(to_value(x) for x in original_strings))
L00296: 
L00297: 
L00298: ################ Check the Predicted Denotations ################
L00299: 
L00300: def check_denotation(target_values, predicted_values):
L00301:     """Return True if the predicted denotation is correct.
L00302:     
L00303:     Args:
L00304:         target_values (list[Value])
L00305:         predicted_values (list[Value])
L00306:     Returns:
L00307:         bool
L00308:     """
L00309:     # Check size
L00310:     if len(target_values) != len(predicted_values):
L00311:         return False
L00312:     # Check items
L00313:     for target in target_values:
L00314:         if not any(target.match(pred) for pred in predicted_values):
L00315:             return False
L00316:     return True
L00317: 
L00318: 
L00319: ################ Batch Mode ################
L00320: 
L00321: def tsv_unescape(x):
L00322:     """Unescape strings in the TSV file.
L00323:     Escaped characters include:
L00324:         newline (0x10) -> backslash + n
L00325:         vertical bar (0x7C) -> backslash + p
L00326:         backslash (0x5C) -> backslash + backslash
L00327: 
L00328:     Args:
L00329:         x (str or unicode)
L00330:     Returns:
L00331:         a unicode
L00332:     """
L00333:     return x.replace(r'\n', '\n').replace(r'\p', '|').replace('\\\\', '\\')
L00334: 
L00335: def tsv_unescape_list(x):
L00336:     """Unescape a list in the TSV file.
L00337:     List items are joined with vertical bars (0x5C)
L00338: 
L00339:     Args:
L00340:         x (str or unicode)
L00341:     Returns:
L00342:         a list of unicodes
L00343:     """
L00344:     return [tsv_unescape(y) for y in x.split('|')]
L00345: 
L00346: def main():
L00347:     parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
L00348:     parser.add_argument('-t', '--tagged-dataset-path',
L00349:             default=os.path.join('.', 'tagged', 'data'),
L00350:             help='Directory containing CoreNLP-tagged dataset TSV file')
